title: Facilitate a 30-minute workshop
why_matters: Your first facilitated meeting is the moment people stop seeing you as new. Keep it short, keep the agenda visible, and finish on time. The half-page of preparation in advance is what makes the meeting look easy. People will remember how it felt to be in the room; that's the metric.
steps: Pick a topic with one specific decision. Examples: which of three approaches we'll pursue, what the acceptance criteria for story X look like, who owns the post-launch review.
Write a half-page agenda the day before. List the decision required, the people you've invited, the order of the conversation, and the rough time per section.
Send the agenda 24 hours ahead. Reread it 30 minutes before. Tweak.
Facilitate. Stick to time. Send the written summary within four hours.
success_criteria: Meeting started on time, ended on time, made the decision it was booked to make. Summary is sent same-day to all attendees. At least one attendee replies acknowledging.
reflection_prompt: What was the moment you most wanted to fill silence — and what would have happened if you had?
